summary: Theodore Dwight Woolsey worked in linguistics and history and archaeology. He was educated at the Hopkins School and studied at Yale College from around 1816 to 1820. He also taught Edward Elbridge Salisbury.

Theodore Gabriel is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He earned an M.Litt from the University of Aberdeen and served as a Lecturer in Religious Studies at the University of Gloucestershire.

Theodore Stcherbatsky was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and philosopher. He studied under Ivan Pavlovich Minaev, Georg Bühler, and Hermann Jacobi, and was attested as a Member of the Russian Academy of Sciences in 1931.
Theophil Gubler was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He completed his doctoral degree at the University of Basel in 1903, having studied under Jacob Wackernagel.

Thich Nhat Hanh was a Buddhist and religious studies figure who studied at Columbia University and Princeton University from 1961 to 1963. He held teaching posts at both institutions in 1961 and founded the School of Youth for Social Service in 1964.
Thich Thien Nghiem is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Delhi under the doctoral supervision of Shalini Singhal, attested in 2012.

Thierry Mathou is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He studied at EDHEC Business School (~1982-1985) and the Paris Institute of Political Studies (~1985-1987), and served as an Associated Political Scientist at the CNRS.

Thierry Meynard is a scholar of sinology and philosophy. He earned a PhD in philosophy at Peking University (~1999-2003) under Yulie Lou, became Professor of Philosophy at Sun Yat-sen University around 2006, and directed The Beijing Center for Chinese Studies in 2012.

Thinh Canh Quang is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of the West, attested in 2007, under doctoral supervisor Kottegoda S. Warnasuriya, having also studied under Lewis Lancaster and Ananda W. P. Guruge.

Thinley Dorji Bhutia worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He taught Tibetan and served as Boarding Superintendent at Darjeeling Government High School, and in 1994 was attested as Director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and Chief Editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology.

Thomas A. Forsthoefel is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He holds degrees from Georgetown University (BA), Loyola University Chicago (MA), and the University of Chicago (PhD under Paul J. Griffiths), and was an associate professor at Mercyhurst University in 2007.

Thomas A. Tweed works in religious and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Stanford University (~1979-1984), with William R. Hutchison as doctoral supervisor, and served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (~1993-2008).

Thomas Borchert is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He was a PhD candidate at the University of Chicago (attested 2005) and held a post as Associate Professor of Religion at the University of Vermont (attested 2017).

Thomas Burrow was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. After attending Queen Elizabeth School, he studied at Christ's College, Cambridge (~1927-1935), and served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Oxford from around 1944 to 1976.
Thomas Cleary worked in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Harvard University from around 1967 to 1975, where he studied under E. Bruce Brooks.
Thomas E. Crow is an art historian and archaeologist who studied at Pomona College (~1965-1969). He held positions at the University of Michigan (~1986-1990) and New York University (~2007).

Thomas Edward Colebrooke was a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. Educated at Eton College and East India Company College, he served as President (1864-1882) and later Vice-President (until 1890) of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

Thomas Freeman Yarnall is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Washington and Columbia University (PhD 2003 under Robert A. F. Thurman), where he was attested in 2007 as Executive Editor in the Department of Religion.

Thomas H. Doctor specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling and conducted doctoral research at the University of Lausanne under Tom J. F. Tillemans, having also received MA supervision from Christian K. Wedemeyer.

Thomas James Mazanec works in sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Calvin University, earned an MA from the University of Colorado Boulder, and completed doctoral work under supervisors Anna M. Shields, Stephen F. Teiser, and Wang Ping, attested in 2017.
